instructions: Put the 1 1/2 cups bulgur in a bowl and cover it with 2 cups cold water. Leave it for 30 minutes, then drain it in a sieve and press out as much water as you can.
While the bulgur soaks, make the filling. Dice about three quarters of the onion. That should be about 1 cup. Keep the rest of the onion for the dough.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Add 8 oz of the beef and 1/2 tsp of the salt, and the 1/4 tsp black pepper. Break the beef up and cook for 5 minutes, until it's deep brown.
Stir in 1/2 tsp of the allspice, 1/2 tsp of the 7 spice and the cinnamon. Cook for 1 minute, until it smells toasty. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the pomegranate molasses.
Spread the filling on a plate and let it cool completely, about 15 minutes.

Grate the remaining quarter of the onion on the big holes of a box grater. Put it in a food processor with the remaining 12 oz beef, 2 tsp salt, the remaining 1/2 tsp allspice, the remaining 1/2 tsp 7 spice, the white pepper and the nutmeg. Pulse until it's a smooth paste.
Add the drained bulgur and pulse until the dough is smooth and sticky. No processor? Knead everything together by hand with wet hands for 5 to 7 minutes.
Set a bowl of cold water beside you. With wet hands, take a piece of dough a little bigger than a golf ball, about 3 tablespoons, and roll it smooth.
Press your thumb into the ball and turn it to make a thin-walled cup. Put a heaping tablespoon of the cool filling inside. Don't overfill it or the ball will split.
Pinch the opening closed and shape the ball into an oval with pointed ends. Set it on a tray and repeat to make about 16.

Chill the tray for 30 minutes so the balls hold together in the oil. To freeze some instead, freeze them on the tray with space between them for 3 hours, then move them to a freezer bag. They keep for 3 months. Thaw them in the fridge overnight before frying.
Pour 3 cups vegetable oil into a heavy pot or deep skillet and heat it over medium-high to 350°F. No thermometer? Drop in a small piece of dough. It should sizzle right away and float.
Fry 4 or 5 balls at a time for about 5 minutes, turning them once, until dark golden brown all over. Cut one open to check. It's done when the shell is cooked through with no raw meat in the middle.
Transfer the balls to paper towels to drain. Serve them hot.
Leftover kibbeh keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat it in a 375°F oven for 10 minutes.
method_notes: Both sources make a lean beef and fine bulgur shell around a browned, spiced beef filling, and fry it in batches. They differ on the filling (one adds pomegranate molasses, the other lamb and a herb mix), so this follows the lead for the filling and shell. Pine nuts are left out of the filling to keep it nut-free. Raw balls freeze well on a tray first, as the second source describes. All ratings are small, so the lead is a fallback. Amounts are scaled down from about 20 balls to 16.
